title: The cheapest order of tools, with the worked example
objectives: Use the four tools in order: new money, redirect income, switch/STP, sell.
Work the example: 64.6% needs nothing; 51.3% needs about ₹1.5 L.
body_md:
The cheapest order of tools. New money first: direct SIPs, bonuses or maturities to the underweight asset. No selling, so no exit load or tax. Redirect income: send IDCW payouts, if any, to the underweight side. Switch or STP within the fund house: for larger gaps, move money in stages. Each switch is a redemption, so check exit load and tax. Sell and reinvest: only for what the first three can't fix. Worked example (illustrative). Client: ₹20 L, target 60% equity / 40% debt, calendar + ±5-point band.

| Step | After a strong equity year (+30%) | After a fall (equity −25%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Equity | ₹15.6 L | ₹9.0 L |
| Debt (+7%) | ₹8.56 L | ₹8.56 L |
| Total | ₹24.16 L | ₹17.56 L |
| Equity share | ≈ 64.6% (+4.6 points) | ≈ 51.3% (−8.7 points) |
| Band breached? | No, within ±5: no action needed, or use new money | Yes: rebalance |
| Action | Optional: ≈ ₹1.8 L of new money (e.g. ₹15,000 a month for a year) to debt brings it to ≈ 60% | Move ≈ ₹1.5 L from debt to equity, in one go or in stages |
example: 64.6% (+4.6 points): no action needed, or ≈ ₹1.8 L of new money (₹15,000 a month for a year) to debt brings it to ≈ 60%. 51.3% (−8.7 points): move ≈ ₹1.5 L from debt to equity, in one go or in stages.
say: New money first: no exit load, no tax.
Switches are redemptions: check load and tax.

check.q: With a ±5-point band, a 60% target at 64.6% means…
check.why: Within band: no action needed. Optional nudge with new money.

o: Directing new money to the underweight asset
check.why: Directing new money to the underweight asset. No exit load, no tax.

check.q: After equity falls 25% (60/40 start), rebalancing means…
o: Moving money from debt to equity
check.why: Moving money from debt to equity. About ₹1.5 L from debt to equity in the example.
